title: Anchor Finger Chord Changes (E, A, D): E to A and E to D using the anchor finger technique
summary: This video demonstrates an anchor-finger approach to smooth chord changes among E, A, and D on the guitar. The technique centers on keeping the first finger as an anchor while sliding it between frets to form the target chords, then dropping the remaining fingers into place (2 and 3 for A or D). The presenter walks through E→A and E→D transitions, emphasizes sliding the anchor finger first, returning to E, and adds guidance on practicing in finger order (1-2-3) and a suggested one-minute drill to build familiarity with the motion before speeding up changes. The guidance focuses on feeling and pattern rather than introducing new guitar shapes beyond those three chords.
topics: placing second and third fingers for new chord
returning to E by lifting 2nd/3rd fingers

sections.title: Chord Changes E - A - E
sections.description: Explains keeping the first finger as an anchor while sliding it to reach the A and D shapes, then lifting the other fingers and returning to E. Shows the exact sequence: slide anchor to the second fret to form A, place fingers 2 and 3 for A, then lift 2 and 3 and slide anchor back to form E; repeat with D by moving the anchor to the second fret, placing 2 and 3 for D, then returning to E. Also covers practicing the motion, and emphasizes starting from the anchor and ordering finger-downs (1-2-3) to build familiarity before committing to simultaneous changes.
